title: Seoul: A Fine Dining Odyssey: Four days of Michelin-starred Korean cuisine, hidden omakase bars, and cultural immersion in one of Asia's greatest food cities
description: Seoul is a city where ancient palaces sit alongside Michelin-starred temples of gastronomy. This luxury solo itinerary is built around Korea's finest dining — from innovative Korean haute cuisine at Jungsik and Mingles to the refined elegance of La Yeon's traditional Korean course meals. Between extraordinary meals, explore Joseon-era palaces, wander through Bukchon's hanok village, sip tea in centuries-old tea houses, and unwind in a traditional jjimjilbang.

days.title: Arrival & Gangnam Gastronomy
days.description: Touch down in Seoul and dive straight into Gangnam's Michelin-starred dining scene after a peaceful temple visit.

activities.name: Arrive at Incheon International Airport
activities.description: Take the AREX express train (43 min, ₩9,500) to Seoul Station, then taxi or metro to your hotel. Settle into your accommodation in the Gangnam or Jongno area. A serene 8th-century Buddhist temple tucked between Gangnam's skyscrapers. Walk the grounds, admire the 23-meter Maitreya Buddha statue, and find calm before your culinary journey begins.

days.title: Palaces, Hanok & Korean Haute Cuisine
days.description: A full day of Joseon-era grandeur, traditional tea culture, and Seoul's most celebrated fine dining — from 2-star Mingles to 3-star La Yeon.

activities.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
activities.description: Seoul's grandest Joseon-era palace (1395). Arrive early for the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony at 10am. Explore the throne hall, Gyeonghoeru Pavilion floating on its lotus pond, and the National Folk Museum inside the grounds.

activities.name: Bukchon Hanok Village
activities.description: Wander through narrow alleys lined with 600-year-old traditional Korean houses (hanok). The area between Gyeongbokgung and Changdeokgung is one of Seoul's most photogenic neighborhoods. A hidden gem — this 1930s wooden hanok was once the home of novelist Lee Tae-jun. Now a traditional tea house serving omija-cha (five-flavor berry tea), daechu-cha (jujube tea), and homemade rice cakes in a magical garden setting.

activities.name: Changdeokgung Palace Moonlight Tour
activities.description: If available (seasonal, limited tickets), this guided nighttime tour through Changdeokgung's Secret Garden is magical — lantern-lit paths through ancient pavilions and 300-year-old trees.

days.title: Itaewon, Markets & Omakase
days.description: From Seoul's oldest market to world-class contemporary art, then sunset at N Seoul Tower and an intimate omakase dinner.

activities.name: Namdaemun Market
activities.description: Seoul's oldest and largest traditional market (est. 1414). Wander through the maze of 10,000+ vendors selling everything from ginseng to handmade knives. The food alley (kalguksu — knife-cut noodle soup) is a must.

activities.name: Leeum Museum of Art
activities.description: Samsung's world-class private art museum in Hannam-dong. Three buildings by Mario Botta, Jean Nouvel, and Rem Koolhaas house Korean national treasures alongside contemporary art. Stunning architecture.

activities.name: Hannam-dong & Itaewon Exploration
activities.description: Stroll through Seoul's most cosmopolitan neighborhood. Browse independent boutiques, specialty coffee shops (try Felt Coffee or Center Coffee), and the vibrant Gyeongnidan-gil street.

activities.name: N Seoul Tower at Sunset
activities.description: Take the Namsan cable car up to Seoul Tower for panoramic views of the city at golden hour. The observation deck offers 360° views across the entire Seoul basin.

days.title: Hongdae, Spa & Grand Finale
days.description: Korean spa culture, indie street art, a 3-star Michelin lunch at Gaon, and a farewell dinner to remember.

activities.name: Dragon Hill Spa (Jjimjilbang)
activities.description: Experience Korea's iconic bathhouse culture at one of Seoul's largest jjimjilbangs. Multiple saunas (charcoal, salt, ice), hot pools, outdoor baths, and a rooftop garden. The quintessential Korean wellness experience.

activities.name: Hongdae Creative District
activities.description: Seoul's indie arts and youth culture hub. Street performers, murals, vinyl shops, and independent designers. Walk through the "Picasso Street" and the Hongdae Free Market (weekends) for handmade goods.

activities.name: Jogyesa Temple
activities.description: Seoul's chief Buddhist temple and headquarters of the Jogye Order. Beautiful in June with lotus lanterns. A moment of zen before your final evening in Seoul. Browse galleries, antique shops, and traditional craft stores. Pick up last-minute souvenirs — Korean celadon ceramics, hanji paper goods, or premium teas.

activities.name: Farewell Cocktails at Charles H.
activities.description: One of Asia's best bars, located in the Four Seasons Seoul. Named after diplomat Charles H. Head, it serves impeccable cocktails in a 1920s-inspired speakeasy setting. The perfect pre-dinner aperitif.
